title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Section 5 (Power to Give Directions)

content.overview: Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the Central Government to issue directions in writing to any person, officer or authority, and such person, officer or authority is bound to comply. Directions may include closure, prohibition or regulation of industry, operation or process, and stoppage or regulation of supply of electricity, water or any other service. Section 5 is a principal enforcement tool linked to s. 3 measures.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is there a written Central direction under s. 5? (2) Who is the addressee? (3) Is the direction within the kinds contemplated (closure/regulation/stoppage of services)? (4) Compliance?
content.study:
s. 5 directions are binding on the addressee. Challenge typically goes to jurisdiction, natural justice and proportionality within public-law limits — without inventing holdings.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Power to direct
sections.body: Central Government may issue written directions to any person, officer or authority; compliance is obligatory.

sections.heading: Scope of directions
sections.body: May include closure, prohibition or regulation of any industry, operation or process; stoppage or regulation of electricity, water or other service supply.

sections.heading: Link to s. 3
sections.body: Directions implement the Central Government's general measures power under s. 3.

sections.heading: Binding effect
sections.body: Addressee is bound to comply; non-compliance attracts the Act's enforcement and penalty scheme.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the direction instrument, addressee, content and compliance status.

examples.title: Closure direction
examples.body: Central Government issues a written s. 5 direction closing a polluting unit and regulating utility supply — addressee is bound to comply.

hypotheticals.question: Can a verbal instruction from a local officer be treated as a s. 5 direction?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 5 contemplates directions in writing by the Central Government (or as the Act/delegation provides); form and authority matter.

distinctions.title: s. 5 directions vs s. 15 penalty
distinctions.right: Penal consequence for contravention of the Act, rules, orders or directions.

misconceptions.trap: Only courts can order industrial closure for pollution.
misconceptions.correction: s. 5 expressly contemplates Central Government directions including closure and regulation of industry, operation or process.
